{"description":"Three small Cargo-level problems.

1. persona-attestors/src/piv.rs:25-34 — both arms of the `pkcs11` cfg return the same value:

       #[cfg(feature = "pkcs11")]
       { /* ponytail comment */ false }
       #[cfg(not(feature = "pkcs11"))]
       false

   The conditional compilation buys nothing: `is_available()` is `false` either way. Enabling the `pkcs11` feature changes no behaviour anywhere in the crate — `enumerate` (line 49) and `prove` (line 55) are unconditional stubs. Same for `goa`: goa.rs:28-34 is the feature's only use, and the crate's `enumerate` returns `Ok(vec![])` regardless. persona-attestors/Cargo.toml:7-9 documents both as placeholders, which is honest, but a feature that cannot change behaviour is a trap — someone will enable `--features pkcs11` and reasonably conclude smartcards are broken rather than unimplemented. Collapse each to a single unconditional `false` until the dependency actually lands, and keep the feature declaration if you want the name reserved.

2. persona-core/Cargo.toml:14 — `serde_json = "1"` is specified inline while every other dependency in the crate uses `.workspace = true`, and the workspace root (Cargo.toml:32) already declares `serde_json = "1"`. Two independent version specs for one dependency; bumping the workspace one silently leaves persona-core behind. Change to `serde_json.workspace = true`.

3. `rustls` is declared by both persona-grpc/Cargo.toml:18 and personad/Cargo.toml:17 and is used by neither. Grep for `rustls` across all .rs files in the workspace returns exactly one hit, and it is inside a comment: personad/src/main.rs:12, the ponytail note about a future axum-plus-rustls HTTP gateway. Both crates pull rustls 0.23 with the ring backend into the build for nothing — build time and audit surface for an unused TLS stack. Remove both declarations; add rustls back when the gateway lands.

(Verified the other suspicious-looking deps are genuinely used: serde_json in personad/src/main.rs:40, libc and sha2 in persona-grpc/src/consumer_attest.rs, tokio-stream in persona/src/main.rs:412.)"}

{"description":"Two Cargo-level problems. (The empty `goa`/`pkcs11` feature flags are persona-5s4b.42 — but note that issue's claim that there is "no cfg(feature = \"goa\") or cfg(feature = \"pkcs11\") anywhere" is not quite right: goa.rs:28-34 and piv.rs:26-33 both do gate on them. The gating is just inert, because in piv.rs both arms return `false` and in goa.rs the `enumerate` stub returns `Ok(vec![])` either way. Same conclusion, different reason.)

1. persona-core/Cargo.toml:14 — `serde_json = "1"` is specified inline while every other dependency in that crate uses `.workspace = true`, and the workspace root already declares `serde_json = "1"` at Cargo.toml:32. Two independent version specs for one dependency: bumping the workspace entry silently leaves persona-core behind, and the divergence is invisible until someone diffs the two manifests. Change to `serde_json.workspace = true`.

2. `rustls` is declared by persona-grpc/Cargo.toml:18 and personad/Cargo.toml:17 and used by neither. Grepping `rustls` across every .rs file in the workspace returns exactly one hit and it is inside a comment — personad/src/main.rs:12, the ponytail note about a future axum-plus-rustls HTTP gateway. Both crates therefore build rustls 0.23 with its ring backend for nothing: build time, plus a TLS stack in the dependency audit surface that no code can reach. Remove both declarations and add rustls back when the gateway lands.

Verified the other plausible-looking candidates are genuinely used, so this is the whole list: serde_json in personad/src/main.rs:40, libc and sha2 in persona-grpc/src/consumer_attest.rs, tokio-stream in persona/src/main.rs:412.","title":"Cargo hygiene: serde_json not inherited, rustls declared but unused"}

rustls deleted from persona-grpc and personad in 39d0331. It was declared, referenced by zero lines of Rust, and pinned to features=["ring"], so removing it was part of dropping ring rather than separate cleanup. The serde_json inheritance half of .104 was fixed earlier.
